A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same generalized score-matching framework and core experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison despite the changed title, formatting, and appendix numbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-data generation, rotated-MNIST experiments, QM9 conformer energies, and CrossDocked docking results in Section 5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds quantitative synthetic-data and MNIST evaluations and a BBDM docking comparison.

M1.justification: The proposed forward/reverse SDEs, generalized-score objective, Algorithms 1–2, and model architectures are unchanged. The representation-space framing explains the existing procedure; the new classifier and docking baseline are evaluation components.

E1.justification: Table 3 adds an explicit 3D Gaussian-mixture evaluation beyond v1's illustrated 2D/4D mixtures and 3D torus/Möbius examples. The added BBDM docking scenario uses rotation-only perturbations alongside the retained rotation-and-translation task. MNIST, QM9, and CrossDocked remain.

E2.justification: v2 adds standard Fisher score matching to the synthetic-data comparisons and BBDM to CrossDocked. These methods appeared elsewhere in v1 but were not evaluated in these corresponding comparisons. Existing MNIST BBDM, QM9 Fisher, and docking RSGM comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v2 introduces prior-normalized Wasserstein-2 evaluation, MNIST classification accuracy and FID using a trained classifier, and docking distance-matrix MAE. Appendix E.3.1 adds a 100-step BBDM protocol with rotation-only endpoints and 3N coordinate outputs, differing from GSM/RSGM's six-dimensional rigid-motion setting. Retained experiments' stated settings are otherwise stable.

E4.justification: Section 5.4 adds an internal-geometry error analysis: BBDM has distance-matrix MAE 0.43 ± 0.21, whereas GSM and RSGM preserve distances by construction. This tests deformation beyond docking RMSD. Existing component-wise synthetic illustrations and MNIST failure examples are retained or refreshed.

E5.justification: Table 1 introduces average-plus/minus summaries for the previously qualitative MNIST comparison, without defining the uncertainty calculation. v2 also explicitly calls docking summaries mean/std. Neither version specifies training seed counts, and both retain five dockings per complex over 100 test complexes.

E6.justification: New MNIST results report GSM/BBDM accuracy 0.96/0.80 and FID 85.8/133.4. Table 3 adds mixed synthetic results, including normalized W2 of 0.34/0.15 for 2D mixtures and 0.14/0.35 for the torus, comparing GSM/Fisher. BBDM docking RMSD 2.92 ± 1.57 Å and deformation errors are newly reported under its rotation-only setting. Existing QM9 energies and GSM/RSGM docking results remain.

T1.justification: Appendix E.1 newly defines an evaluation quantity by dividing generated-to-target W2 by target-to-prior W2. This is a limited mathematical definition. The Lie-group conditions, propositions, main theorem and proofs, and flow-matching derivation remain substantively unchanged after matching appendix and equation renumbering.

C1.justification: The introduction removes the specific first-method and first-denoising-result priority assertions for simulation-free/non-Abelian diffusion, while retaining the underlying capabilities. The headline framing emphasizes Lie-group representations. Exact SDEs, dimensionality reduction, distribution bridging, and the flow-matching extension remain claimed contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly limits the full theory to vector-space actions, identifies finite groups as unsupported, and clarifies orbit confinement without homogeneity. It adds interpretations concerning prior similarity, symmetry benefits, and docking rigidity. However, Appendix E.1's claim that Fisher wins on Gaussian mixtures conflicts with Table 3's 3D values, 0.40 for GSM versus 0.44 for Fisher.

D1.justification: Appendix E adds the MNIST evaluator's architecture, optimizer, training budget, and FID feature layer, plus the docking BBDM construction and output dimensions. v2 supplies a named repository location instead of only a generic future release promise; the PDF still describes availability prospectively. Existing method implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 removes Bertolini et al. (2024) on contextual molecular explanations and softens the introduction's specific priority claims. The remaining cited literature and principal relationships to equivariant networks, Riemannian diffusion, and flow matching are substantially retained.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, rewrites the introductory explanation around representation-space diffusion, reorganizes related-work paragraphs, and adds a notation appendix and Code Availability section. Most technical exposition and appendix derivations remain closely matched; the revision is not a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the opening conceptual diagram, refreshes MNIST examples and labels in Figure 6, and expands Figure 8 with BBDM distributions. It introduces three tables covering MNIST metrics, notation, and synthetic results. Conference formatting and substantial resizing/text wrapping also change the presentation of retained figures.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the previously qualitative toy-data and MNIST validation more assessable, adds a useful docking deformation diagnostic, and improves evaluation documentation and scope qualifications. These gains are limited by the Table 3 discussion inconsistency, unexplained MNIST uncertainty summaries, and unequal perturbation settings in the new docking comparison. The core method and theoretical support remain unchanged, yielding a useful but bounded overall improvement.
